inspiration: Procedural dungeon by time window: the dungeon module makes rooms lazily, only when a player walks through a new exit, and tags each room with an instance id tied to a time window, so people who go the same way within the window share a branch. Recreate with our own theme and rules; the docstring says the way back to the start room becomes a one-way exit, a rule we may change. Reference: evennia/contrib/tutorials/evadventure/dungeon.py (module docstring, lines 1-12).

Rune-stone spells as items: each magic effect is a consumable stone item with its own base class, so casting is a use-item action with stored charges. Recreate with our own spell carriers (carved glyph, tattoo, brand) and different use rules. Reference: evennia/contrib/tutorials/evadventure/objects.py line 287 (base class docstring).

Inventory as slots: the inventory has slots, and filling them changes how well a character does things, which gives a light weight system with no arithmetic. Recreate with weight by stance or by hands used, not by slot count. Reference: evennia/contrib/tutorials/evadventure/equipment.py line 2 (module docstring).

Builder detail keywords on rooms: a builder can attach a description to a keyword on a room, so examine returns extra text without new objects. Recreate with auto-generated details from room tags, plus our own keyword rules. Reference: evennia/contrib/tutorials/tutorial_world/rooms.py lines 94-125 (CmdTutorialSetDetail).

Character creation from tables: a chargen table set rolls a virtue, a vice, an alignment and start gear from lists, so a sheet is generated and then edited. Recreate with our own tables and no names from the source tables. Reference: evennia/contrib/tutorials/evadventure/random_tables.py line 8 (chargen_tables) and chargen.py.

Two combat modes on one ruleset: a turn-based module and a twitch module sit beside a shared combat base module, so a game can pick either. Recreate with our own timing rules. Reference: evennia/contrib/tutorials/evadventure/combat_turnbased.py and combat_twitch.py (names only; bodies not read; the shared base is combat_base.py).

briefs.label: Time-window branch dungeon
briefs.why: Players who take the same door within a short window share one dungeon branch and end up together, which makes group play feel shared without a lobby. One signature behaviour: a door that spawns a new branch on a timer.
briefs.keep: kept: rooms generated only when first walked into; an instance tag per time window; shared branches for the people who go the same way.
briefs.change: changed: our own theme and room grammar, a different window rule (per party, not per door), and the return path rule. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.

briefs.label: Stone-glyph spell item
briefs.why: A spell that is a physical item with charges is easy to read at 375 wide in an inventory list and gives players something to trade or lose. One signature effect: casting uses up the item.
briefs.keep: kept: a magic effect as a consumable item with its own base class and charges.
briefs.change: changed: our own carrier (carved glyph, tattoo, brand), our own use rules (cooldown per carrier, not a stack), and a new name set. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.

briefs.label: Slot-weighted pack
briefs.why: A pack where filling slots makes a character worse at things is a visible, low-maths way to show load. One signature behaviour: a near-full pack changes the character's stance in the text.
briefs.keep: kept: inventory slots that change how well the character does things.
briefs.change: changed: our own penalty (by hands used or stance), a different slot count, and a readout that uses our own words. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.

briefs.label: Keyword detail on a room
briefs.why: Examine text on a few hidden keywords makes a room feel dense without extra objects. One signature behaviour: a hidden keyword reveals a line when examined.
briefs.keep: kept: builder-set keyword details on a room, with aliases.
briefs.change: changed: details generated from our own room tags, and a reveal that depends on time or light. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
